# Integration Points

## HashiCorp Vault

Vault Enterprise 1.21 introduced a native SPIFFE auth method, reaching general
availability in October 2025 [13][30]. This supports both JWT and X.509
certificate-based authentication [13]. OIDC federation via the JWT auth method
provides a non-enterprise path [14].

Vault can also serve as an upstream authority, with its PKI secrets engine
signing SPIRE intermediate CAs.

The OIDC authentication flow proceeds: workload requests JWT-SVID from the local
SPIRE Agent, presents it to Vault's JWT auth method, receives a Vault token, and
uses that token to access secrets [14].

## Istio Service Mesh

SPIRE replaces the default Istio CA (istiod) via the Envoy SDS API [9]. The
SPIFFE CSI driver mounts the SDS socket into workload pods [5].

Istio integration imposes strict requirements: the SPIFFE ID must follow the
format `spiffe://<trust.domain>/ns/<ns>/sa/<sa>` [9], and the socket must be
mounted at the path `/var/run/secrets/workload-spiffe-uds/socket` [9].

Istio Ambient mode uses ztunnel as a SPIRE delegate through the DelegatedIdentity
API, enabling per-node identity management without sidecar injection.

## Sigstore Supply Chain Security

The Teleport implementation demonstrates merging workload identity with software
supply chain security. A SigstorePolicy configuration resource enables
policy-driven artifact signing using SPIFFE-issued credentials.

## OpenTelemetry

ZTWIM enables secretless observability pipelines via X.509 mTLS. ClusterSPIFFEID
CRDs template identities for OTEL collectors. A multi-hop identity chain using
the x-spiffe-id HTTP header propagates workload identity through collector
pipelines. TLS 1.3 is the only supported protocol version [19].

## Validated Patterns

The Layered Zero Trust validated pattern combines ZTWIM with Vault, Keycloak,
External Secrets Operator, and the Compliance Operator to provide a
comprehensive zero trust stack [11].

## Gaps and Limitations

1. No native SPIFFE authentication existed in Vault before Enterprise 1.21,
   requiring workarounds through OIDC/JWT auth methods.
2. Macquarie Bank found that integrating SPIRE with Vault required building a
   custom event-driven system because Vault entities lacked sufficient context
   and the JWT sub claim could not be modified [27].
3. Istio's hardcoded SAN validation prevents transparent multi-trust-domain
   operation [28].
